task.description: Record the ISS-0152 outcome in CHANGELOG.md, verify requirement mapping, update docs/issues/ISS-0152.json with status/resolution/prevention and cross-references to ISS-0180 and ISS-0181.
acceptance_criteria: CHANGELOG.md states accurately that #484's symptom was already resolved by #499, that the underlying T010 debt is carried to #512, and that #511 was found
CHANGELOG.md does not claim any test source was fixed by this run
Requirement mapping checked against docs/requirements.yaml, not assumed
docs/issues/ISS-0152.json status RESOLVED with evidence, prevention, and cross-references

result.summary: CHANGELOG.md records ISS-0152 under a 'Verified (no code change)' heading, stating explicitly that this run changed no test source, no linter and no baseline, and why that is the correct output: the reported C5 failure was already fixed by ISS-0171/PR #499 and is not reproducible on a pristine main worktree (HEAD b2cc55c, linter exit 0). The gate-gaming audit of #499's baseline regeneration is recorded (225 entries before and after, 0 newly suppressed, 0 disappeared when diffed on (severity, code, file, message) ignoring line) along with the environment cause of the local exit 1 (BPM_TEST_DB_URL shadowed to port 5434 instead of 5453, plus 2 unapplied migrations) - which was C4, not C5. The residual debt is stated at its true size (184 raw T010 findings across 45 files, up from 88 because PR #490 wired 55 orphaned test files into build targets) and carried to ISS-0181/GH #512; the new gate-integrity defect is recorded as ISS-0180/GH #511. Requirement mapping was checked, not assumed: a keyword scan of all 359 entries in docs/requirements.yaml surfaced ENV-01/ENV-02 as the only near matches, and reading both shows they govern tenant-level production/test isolation, not test-fixture isolation - so no requirement maps and no status was moved. docs/issues/ISS-0152.json is RESOLVED with full evidence, 5-point prevention text, and cross-references to ISS-0171/#499, ISS-0180/#511, ISS-0181/#512 and GH #490.
